full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 13-8-1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 97 of 1991 dismissing the appellant's application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 "In any case in which a decree is passed ex parte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside; and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as against' him upon such term as to costs, payment into Court or otherwise as it thinks fit, and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit: 

 6. In deciding a case under Order 9 rule I3 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court is required to consider two questions: (1) whether summons was duly served upon the defendants or (2) whether the defendants were prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for ex parte hearing. When the Court is satisfied that petitioners have been able to prove either of the two conditions it is bound to set aside the ex parte decree. 

 7. From the impugned order it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge has totally ignored the provision of Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in deciding the case. He does not appear to have at all applied his judicial mind to investigate and determine the basic questions involved in the case before him under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Admittedly, the suit was dismissed for default on 23-9-1989 and thereafter it was restored to its original file and number on 30-11-89 in the absence of the defendants, on the application filed by the plaintiffs under Order 9 rule 4 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is also an undisputed fact that after the restoration of the suit to its original file and number on 30-11-1989 no fresh notice was served upon the defendants intimating them of the next date of hearing of the suit. After the dismissal of the suit on 30-11-89 a valuable right accrued in favour of the defendants and, in all fairness, it was just and legitimate that the defendants should have been notified about the next date of hearing of the suit after the dismissal of the suit was set aside in their absence and beyond their knowledge. The learned Subordinate Judge himself found in the impugned order that when the suit was dismissed under Order 9 rule 4 CPC the defendants were entitled to a notice about the next date of hearing but subsequently he retracted from that stand on untenable grounds. 

 8. Although Order 9 rule 2 or 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure appears to be silent on the question of a fresh notice upon the defendants after the restoration of a suit to its original file and number, Mr. Farooque Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the appellant, submits that equity and justice demand that a fresh notice upon the defendants is absolutely necessary for preventing an injustice. Mr Farooque Ahmed has referred to the case of MooI Chand vs. Ganga Sahai, reported in AIR 1933 Al, 522 and the case of Ram Chandra Ramaji Khatik and others vs. Shahadeo Gopala Koshti and others, reported in AIR 1945, Nagpur, 185 in support of his submissions. In these cases their Lordships held that after restoration of a suit under Order 9 rule 4 CPC the defendants are entitled both in equity and as of right to notice of the date fixed for hearing of the suit after its restoration on setting aside of the order of dismissal for default. 

 "Where a suit is dismissed under rule 2 or rule 3, the plaintiff may (subject to the law of limitation) bring a fresh -suit: or he may apply for an order to set the dismissal aside, and if he satisfies the Court that there was sufficient cause for his not paying the court-fee and postal charges (if any) required within the time fixed before the issue of the summons, or for his non-appearance, as the case may be, the Court shall make an order setting aside the dismissal and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit." 

 10. Against the ex parte dismissal of a suit under rule 2 or rule 3 of Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure the plaintiff has two remedies open to him (1) he may bring a fresh suit or (2) he may apply for an order to set the dismissal aside. Order 9, rule 4 provides that if the plaintiff can satisfy the Court that there was sufficient cause for the default leading to the dismissal of the suit, the Court shall make an order setting aside the dismissal and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit. Since two courses are open to the plaintiff against the ex parte dismissal of the suit the defendant is not supposed to know the remedy actually availed of by the plaintiff in this regard, unless notified. Moreover, with the dismissal of the suit, albeit ex parte, a valuable right accrued to the defendants and that right, in all fairness, cannot be taken away without affording them an opportunity of being heard. Since the restoration of the suit took place behind the back and beyond the know lege of the defendants and they had no occasion to know about it, the defendants became entitled both in equity and as of right to notice of the date fixed for hearing of the suit after its restoration at the instance of the plaintiff. Principles of natural justice, equity and good conscience do come in aid of the defendant under such circumstances. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it must be held that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 rule 13 CPC when the suit was called on for hearing on 7-6-1990 and ex parte decree passed. 

 12. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned order dated 13-8-1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka is set aside and the appellant's application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC is allowed and the ex parte decree dated 7-6-1990 passed in Title Suit No. 399 of 1987 by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka is set aside. The learned Subordinate Judge is directed to proceed with the suit in accordance with law. Since this is a very old case the learned Subordinate Judge is directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously, preferably within six months, from the date of receipt of this order.
